before.label: Hemp bundle
before.description: Fibres for making a coil of binding rope.

before.label: Twisting stick
before.description: A reusable tool for twisting fibres into rope.

before.label: Rope coil
before.description: The coil you made has enough binding rope for both carriers. Individual lengths tie boards or bind the woven willow; the shared coil remains.

before.label: Board kit
before.description: Prepared boards and their fasteners, enough for one closed crate.

before.label: Willow bundle
before.description: Flexible willow, enough for one open-weave basket.

before.label: Closed crate
before.description: A sturdy carrier with a closed bottom. It holds coarse stones and fine sand.

before.label: Open-weave basket
before.description: A sturdy carrier. Its woven gaps hold coarse stones but let fine sand fall through.

before.label: Hand drill
before.description: A reusable tool for making small holes in wood.

before.label: Perforated crate
before.description: The same crate, now pierced with small holes. Coarse gravel stays; fine sand falls through.

before.label: Sandy gravel
before.description: The load brought back from the quarry: coarse gravel mixed with fine sand.

before.label: Sorted gravel
before.description: The coarse gravel remains after the fine sand falls through the sieve.

after.label: Copper basin blank
after.description: A partly formed copper blank with two pierced rim tabs. The fixed forming block belongs to the workbench.

after.label: Wooden mallet
after.description: The workshop mallet can finish the prepared copper blank. It remains an ordinary wooden mallet afterward.

after.label: Copper washbasin
after.description: The same copper blank, finished as a washbasin with two pierced rim tabs.

after.label: Crossbar, hooks and cords
after.description: A prepared crossbar with two suspension hooks and cords for the basin rim tabs, an upper mounting loop for the gatepost bracket, and a loose tether for a striker.

after.label: Hanging basin gong
after.description: The same copper basin hangs from its rim tabs on the crossbar. The loose tether can keep a striker beside it.

before.label: Quarry gate
before.description: Bring a stone carrier here. The path makers take it on the collection trip and return it with gravel.

after.label: Washing bench
after.description: The painter has the rinse water and brushes ready here.

after.label: Outside gatepost bracket
after.description: A fixed bracket outside the gate, within visitors’ reach.

before: Research probe, not a promoted campaign or a human-tested game.
Both initial forms carry stones; both open forms sieve gravel. No quota, cost, or exclusive-choice rule.
The basket route needs no alteration; drilling preserves the same crate but removes its fine-sand containment property.
Every later successful route uses an earlier-made carrier or the earlier-made rope to produce another fitting carrier.
The three crafting steps and quarry trip compress fictional skilled work; this is not construction guidance or simulated physics.
No output flags represent explanations. The end is in the scene, not an ingredient.
after: Isolated content-level probe; fictional craft compression, not practical metalworking instructions.
The gust, clang, brush washing and visitor response are authored narrative events. No wind, acoustics or human behaviour is simulated.
Visible stage motivation carries the incident; generic item descriptions are not automatically shown by the current UI.
No purpose tokens, finite resource accounting, score trade-off, hidden intention state or new runtime mechanic.
The requested mounted fixture is one design, not a claim that a handheld basin could never call anyone.

before: We need a sturdy carrier for coarse stones. Bring one to the quarry gate.

before: The carrier returns with its load. Your rope coil and spare materials come to the mason’s yard too.
after: Carry the washbasin and the same wooden mallet outside.

before: The returned load is tipped out beside a hand drill.
after: The keeper brings a crossbar, hooks and cords. The hooks fit the basin’s two pierced rim tabs; the upper loop fits the outside gatepost bracket. A loose tether can hold a striker.

before: The sand falls away. The gravel is ready for the path.
after: An arriving visitor lifts the tethered mallet and strikes your hanging basin. Its clear clang reaches the back room. The keeper comes out and opens the gate.

before: The load is full of fine sand. I need the coarse gravel: let the sand fall through, but keep the stones.
after: The brushes are clean. Your emptied basin leans beside the gate to dry. A gust rocks it against the iron latch; its clang brings the keeper out. “Visitors knock, but I cannot hear them from the back room. Leave a hanging call signal outside the gate, with something for them to strike it with.”
